name: Trinity Catholic High School
notes: SEED ERRORS CORRECTED: seed's opened=1957 and closed=2025 are both wrong. Trinity Catholic High School was established in fall 2003 by the merger of St. Thomas Aquinas-Mercy High School and Rosary High School, on the former Rosary campus at 1720 Redman Rd (the Rosary building opened 1961; 'built in 1959' per the archdiocesan paper's closure article). Closure announced February 2021 after an archdiocesan financial feasibility study; last graduating class was 2021 (end of 2020-21 school year), per St. Louis Review, St. Louis Post-Dispatch (B. Bernhard), and KSDK. It was the last high school in St. Louis County directly administered by the Archdiocese. No successor school — students dispersed to other area Catholic schools. Seed's '1957' likely conflates the building/predecessor lineage: Mercy HS (1948, Sisters of Mercy, University City) merged with St. Thomas Aquinas HS (founded 1954 at Sacred Heart Parish, Florissant; moved to Dunn Rd 1958) in 1985 to form St. Thomas Aquinas-Mercy; that entity merged with Rosary HS (opened 1961, School Sisters of Notre Dame) to create Trinity in 2003. ZIP is 63138 (Spanish Lake), not seed's 63135. For yearbook purposes, predecessor schools (Rosary 'Rosarian', Aquinas, Mercy, Aquinas-Mercy) are distinct institutions with their own series.

name: Ferguson Public School District
historical_names: School District of the City of Ferguson
notes: District formation confirmed by the 1948 Ferguson High School 'Crest' yearbook history page: 'The first School Board in Ferguson was appointed in 1867 when a one-room public school was built on the south side of Wesley Avenue... The district was known as District 3 Township 46 as Ferguson was not incorporated. The first School Board for the School District of the City of Ferguson was selected in 1903 when the district was incorporated.' Merger date: the St. Louis County reorganization vote of October 1951 (SLU PRiME Center) created Ferguson-Florissant R-2; the McCluer HS history records '1952 saw the merger of the Ferguson Public School District and the Florissant School District' — the 1951 vote / 1952 operational start explains the seed's 1952, kept as probable. Member schools at merger included Central School (1880, 201 Wesley Ave; renamed from Ferguson School in 1903), John M. Vogt High School (1930, 200 Church Ave; first dedicated HS building), and Ferguson High School (1939, 701 January Ave, WPA-built), plus elementary schools. All absorbed into Ferguson-Florissant R-2 (ALL-453).

name: Ferguson-Florissant School District - Ferguson Schools
notes: Formed by the October 1951 St. Louis County reorganization vote that merged the Ferguson and Florissant districts into Ferguson-Florissant R-2 (SLU PRiME Center); official legal name is 'Ferguson Reorganized School District R-2' (FFSD 2023-24 Annual Budget). Commonly dated 1952 (year the merged district began operating). On June 7, 1975 a U.S. district court ordered FFSD to annex the Berkeley and Kinloch school districts (desegregation order, affirmed at 515 F.2d 1365). Still operating ~22 schools (fergflor.org): current member schools include McCluer HS, McCluer North HS, STEAM Academy at McCluer South-Berkeley, Ferguson MS, Cross Keys MS, STEAM Academy MS, Johnson-Wabash and Wedgwood 6th Grade Centers, Berkeley/Combs/Griffith/Halls Ferry/Lee-Hamilton/Robinwood Intermediates, and Bermuda/Central/Commons Lane/Duchesne/Holman/Parker Road/Walnut Grove Primaries, plus Mark Twain alternative program. This is a district-level row for search routing only — the real yearbook-producing entities are its member schools (Ferguson HS ALL-416/417-era, Vogt, Central, McCluer, McCluer North, etc., most with their own rows in other batches).

name: Florissant School District
notes: District formation date not found online — Florissant had public schooling from the early 19th century (the Combs Elementary seed row notes a Florissant public elementary at the Combs site from 1876; Sacred Heart Academy dates to 1819 but is a private predecessor). The public 'Florissant School District' was among the districts merged by the October 1951 reorganization vote into Ferguson-Florissant R-2 (SLU PRiME Center); 1952 is the commonly cited merger/operational year (McCluer HS history: '1952 saw the merger of the Ferguson Public School District and the Florissant School District'). Member schools at merger included Florissant High School (later repurposed; Florissant HS appears in alumni lists as defunct) and Florissant elementary/junior-high schools — full member list not determined online. Human follow-up: St. Louis County or FFSD board minutes could pin down the district's legal formation date.

name: Hazelwood East High School - Split Session
notes: Real transitional arrangement, not a separate school building: Hazelwood East was established in 1974, and its classes of 1975 and 1976 attended split-day sessions in the existing Hazelwood High School building (East + West students mornings, Central students afternoons) until East's own facility at 11300 Dunn Rd opened fall 1976. The district's own Hazelwood Central history page says East and West opened in 1977 — 1976 (school's Wikipedia history) vs 1977 (district page) conflict kept this row's close-year at probable. SEED ADDRESS LIKELY WRONG: seed gives 1865 Dunn Rd, but the 'existing Hazelwood High School building' in 1974-76 was the second Hazelwood HS at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd (the 1865 Dunn Rd building ceased being the high school in 1966). Successor is the continuing Hazelwood East High School at its own campus (seed row ALL-064, Hazelwood East High School — in another batch).

name: Hazelwood High School - Original Campus
notes: First Hazelwood High School building, completed 1954 at 1865 Dunn Rd (Spanish Lake), per Hazelwood Central's official About Us page and Wikipedia's Hazelwood Central article. It was the district's only high school until the second Hazelwood HS opened in 1966, at which point the high school program moved to the new building — 'closed' here means ceased operating as the high school; the building itself stayed in district use (later Hazelwood Opportunity Center). Successor is the continuing high school at its second campus — seed rows ALL-021 'Hazelwood High School - Second Building' and ALL-022 'Hazelwood Central High School' (other batches) are the same institution; ALL-022 is the present-day name. DUPLICATE FLAG: ALL-459 is effectively the same entity as ALL-020 'Hazelwood High School - Original' (1954-1965) in another batch — kept separate per no-silent-merge rule; recommend aggregation-level merge.

name: Hazelwood Central High School - Dunn Road Campus
notes: SEED ERRORS: this row's address (1865 Dunn Rd) and close year (1977) are wrong. The second Hazelwood High School — renamed Hazelwood Central once the 'Central' designator appeared ~1974 — was built 1965 and opened 1966 at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd (Florissant 63031), where it still operates today as Hazelwood Central High School (chs.hazelwoodschools.org, NCES 291383000622). It held 2,515 students (grades 10-12) its first year, ran split double-shift sessions from 1970, and returned to a conventional schedule in 1977 when Hazelwood East and West opened — 1977 is likely the source of the seed's erroneous 'closed 1977'. DUPLICATE FLAG: same institution as ALL-021 'Hazelwood High School - Second Building' and ALL-022 'Hazelwood Central High School' in other batches — kept separate per no-silent-merge rule; recommend merge at aggregation. The 1865 Dunn Rd address belongs to ALL-459 (original campus, later Hazelwood Opportunity Center).

name: Twillman School - 1928 Building
notes: School's own history page: the original Twillman School was a one-room schoolhouse constructed in 1850 (Twillman family paid the teacher's salary the first year); 'around 1928 a new three-room building was built at 11831 Bellefontaine Rd' — matches the seed's 1928 building; the current facility's biggest remodel was in 1975-76 and the 1928 building was incorporated into it. Twillman Elementary still operates at that address. Seed's 1928 kept as probable ('around 1928' per the school). DUPLICATE FLAG: same school as ALL-075 'Twillman School' (other batch, opened 'Unknown'/closed '1950s?' — the 1950s close guess is wrong; Twillman never closed) — kept separate per review rules; recommend merge. Named for the Twillman(n) family whose 1870 brick homestead stands at 11840 Bellefontaine Rd (Spanish Lake Community Association; Pipes Family Foundation).

name: Fort Bellefontaine Campus
historical_names: St. Louis Boys' Training School / Bellefontaine detention home (site, 1913)
district_operator: Missouri Division of Youth Services (Dept. of Social Services)
notes: SEED OPERATOR ERROR: NCES lists 'fort bellefontaine campus' under the statewide DIVISION OF YOUTH SERVICES district (CCD district 2900009), not Hazelwood School District — a small state-run juvenile residential school (12 students, grades 6-12, 2024-25 CCD). The Missouri DSS DYS FY2019 budget book lists it as a 2-group 'Moderate Care' facility at 13290 Bellefontaine Rd. Site lineage: City of St. Louis acquired the old Fort Belle Fontaine grounds in 1913 and built a boys' detention/training school complex (Photoflood STL); St. Louis County assumed control of most of the property in 1986 and it became a DYS campus ('Missouri Hills Home' era per FortWiki) — probable, secondary sources; exact year the 'Fort Bellefontaine Campus' school program itself began is not documented online. ALL-470 'Fort Bellefontaine School' is almost certainly the same entity under its older name (same address) — flag for merge. Yearbook production unlikely (tiny residential unit) but left to Track B.
